chunks: ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he asked him about a man who buys a one-eyed sacrificial animal and does not come to know of its defect until after purchasing it: would it suffice for him? He said:
Yes, unless it is an obligatory hady, for a deficient one does not suffice.

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةَ: the sacrificial animal offered for udhiyah
key_terms.الْعَوْرَاءَ: one-eyed; an animal having a visible defect
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering, especially in the context of hajj
key_terms.يُجْزِي: suffices or fulfills the legal requirement

ai.seo_question: Does a defective sacrificial animal count if its defect is discovered only after purchase?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a sacrificial animal discovered to have a defect after purchase. It states that such an animal may suffice in general, but if it is an obligatory hady, a defective animal is not valid.
